_comment: Permission profile for the `assistant` session: it watches one other
session's transcript and speaks when that transcript contradicts a claim
It reads and it messages. That is the whole loop, so the allow list is the
whole loop and nothing else. A watcher with a broad grant is a second
session holding your credentials and sitting idle most of the day.
Note the failure mode of a tight allow list on a background session: a
command that is neither allowed nor denied falls through to asking, and
nobody is at a prompt to answer, so it stalls rather than refusing. That is
survivable for this role, because a stalled watcher says nothing and saying
nothing is its normal output. It would not be survivable for a worker.
The denies are already unreachable from the allow list. They are written
anyway: a deny is a statement of intent that survives somebody widening the
allows later, and this role must never become a way to launder an action
the watched session was blocked from taking itself.
